evals.prompt: I'm building a Next.js admin dashboard. Build a page with a table showing customer orders (order id, customer name, total, status). We don't have the backend API yet, but I want it ready to plug in later without rewriting the page.
evals.expected_output: A table component driven by a hook/store backed by a repository interface, with a mock implementation only, realistic-looking varied mock order data (not 'Item 1'/'Item 2'), loading/error/empty states handled, no hardcoded rows in JSX, and a distinctive (non-generic-SaaS-table) visual treatment.

evals.prompt: Add a product grid to the storefront homepage — image, name, price, add-to-cart button, maybe 12-20 products. Backend isn't ready, just use placeholder data for now but make it swappable later.
evals.expected_output: Product data comes from a repository-backed hook, not an inline array in the component. Mock data has varied/realistic product names and prices, not 'Product 1'. Grid handles empty/loading/error states. Visual design avoids generic SaaS-card/e-commerce-template defaults (uniform rounded cards, identical shadow, etc).

evals.prompt: Build a settings page with a list of team members (name, email, role) that I can remove people from. Make the UI look distinctive, not just another generic SaaS table.
evals.expected_output: Team member list backed by repository/mock pattern with remove functionality wired through the same data layer (not just local array splicing disconnected from the data source). Design is deliberately distinctive per frontend-design principles, not a default SaaS list. Accessibility basics present (labels, focus states) per web-design-guidelines.
